articles.title: MG Hector Tomahawk EV with 517km range, PHEV with 1100km+ range launched starting ...
articles.content: JSW MG Motor India has unveiled the Hector Tomahawk, its first product based on the ADAPT (Advanced Drive Architecture Platform Technology) and India’s first Multi-New Energy Vehicle (NEV) platform. It is offered with Electric Vehicle (EV) and Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEV) powertrains. Design and interior The Hector Tomahawk measures 4,745 mm long, 2,130 mm wide including mirrors and 1,770 mm tall, with a 2,810 mm wheelbase and 230 mm ground clearance at the battery. MG says it is the tallest and among the longest vehicles in its segment. Exterior features include sculpted bumpers, Beacon Lights, an illuminated MG logo, Rotor alloy wheels, character lines and an Automatic Power Tailgate. The EV is available in 5- and 7-seater versions, while the PHEV is a 7-seater. The Desert Squadron cabin uses an Almond Brown and Carbon Black theme with leatherette seats, door armrests and dashboard inserts, plus a leather-wrapped steering wheel. Front ventilated seats include 6-way power adjustment for the driver and 4-way power adjustment for the co-driver. The driver seat adds memory and auto-retract functions, while all windows get one-touch auto up/down with anti-pinch protection. The second row has a 60:40 split, recline, slide and tip-and-tumble functions. The 5-seater offers up to 610 litres of boot space, while folding the second and third rows in the 7-seater expands cargo capacity. Cabin features: Dual-pane panoramic Cockpit SkyRoof 15.6-inch (39.62 cm) HD Grand View Display 8.8-inch Multi Information Display 10-speaker Infinity audio Rear window sunshades Storage spaces PM2.5 air filtration 256-colour ambient lighting Dual B-pillar coat hooks Powertrain and range Model Powertrain Battery Motor Range Hector Tomahawk EV Electric 69.2kWh PMSM, 150kW, 310Nm 517km Hector Tomahawk PHEV 1.5-litre petrol + DHT 20.5kWh 148kW 115km+ electric; 1,100km+ combined The EV supports DC fast charging at up to 90kW. The PHEV reaches 0-100km/h in approximately 9 seconds. Its DHT uses an electromagnetic clutch with a claimed 0.1-second response time, while the Motor Control Unit (MCU) has a maximum claimed efficiency of 99.1%. IGBT technology is used for energy management. The Intelligent Energy Management System supports four modes: Pure Electric Drive, Series Hybrid Drive, Parallel Hybrid Drive and Engine Direct Drive. The SUV also supports Vehicle-to-Home (V2H), which MG describes as India’s first such capability, allowing the battery to power appliances, outdoor equipment and homes. Battery safety and warranty The 69.2kWh MAGIC Battery uses high-thermal-stability cell materials, ceramic insulation layers and a high-temperature-resistant electrolyte. Testing includes: Full needle penetration without fire 180-degree thermal shock 55-degree short-circuit testing without abnormality Up to 40% cell deformation without fire or explosion 2,000+ bench tests 490+ full-vehicle validation tests Environmental testing at extreme temperatures, high altitudes and severe cold The Battery Management System monitors battery health in real time, 24/7. The first owner gets a lifetime battery warranty on both EV and PHEV. Connected features The i-SMART 3.0 platform offers 80+ smart features, including i-SWIPE two-, three- and five-finger gestures and a GenAI-powered voice assistant with natural conversation support and 30+ Hinglish voice commands. articles.title: Coal Ministry advisor reviews India's first underground coal gasification project in Kasta
articles.content: Union Ministry of Coal Advisor B. Veera Reddy paid a visit to the Underground Coal Gasification (UCG) Pilot Research & Development (R&D) Project at Kasta, Jharkhand, on Tuesday. The project, managed by the Asansol-based Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL), marks the state’s first underground-coal-to-gasification initiative and serves as India’s premier pilot project for the technology. Upon his arrival, Reddy was received by a delegation of senior ECL executives, including Amitava Bhattacharyya, Area General Manager of ECL’s Pandaveswar Area; Bhaskar Bhattacharya, General Manager (Geology, MCP & NI); and Swarup Kr. Dutta, General Manager (Operations) for the Pandaveswar Area. Advertisement During the visit, Reddy inspected the project site to evaluate its current implementation status. Senior management from ECL and technical representatives from Ergo Exergy Technologies Inc. (EETI), Canada, provided a comprehensive briefing on the various functional units of the pilot plant. Advertisement The Kasta block (Kasta West) development—spanning the Raniganj and Pandaveswar areas across the West Bengal and Jharkhand borders, is being executed as a strategic R&D initiative. The venture is funded directly by the Coal India Limited (CIL) R&D Board as a targeted research scheme rather than drawing from broader commercial surface gasification capital incentive packages. While it functions under CIL backing, the exact financial capital costs have not been publicly itemised in official releases. The project is being jointly spearheaded by ECL and the Central Mine Planning and Design Institute (CMPDI, Ranchi), which acts as the principal implementing agency. Technical expertise is provided via a collaboration with Canada’s EETI. The initiative is structured as a two-year, two-phase programme designed to establish technical feasibility and achieve pilot-scale in-situ syngas production. Following its initial launch with exploratory drilling on June 22, 2024, the project is now successfully nearing the completion of its trial phases. It will soon transition into initial commercial evaluation phases, marking a significant milestone in India’s pursuit of alternative and cleaner coal utilisation technologies. Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL) is planning a surface coal gasification project at Sonepur Bazari in West Bengal, which is expected to become operational in about a year. Developed through a joint venture between Coal India Limited and GAIL at an estimated cost of Rs 13,052.8 crore, the project will produce synthetic natural gas (SNG). Additionally, ECL has been awarded India’s first underground coal gasification project by the Ministry of Coal. Trial work is currently underway, and commercial production is projected to start within a couple of months. These projects align with the National Coal Gasification Mission, which aims to achieve 100 million tonnes (MT) of coal and lignite gasification by 2030—equivalent to nearly half of India’s total coal production. According to Satish Chandra Jha, CMD of ECL, this initiative is designed to cut India’s reliance on imported LNG, urea, ammonia, and methanol. To support these efforts, the Union Cabinet has approved a financial incentive framework worth Rs 37,500 crore for surface coal and lignite gasification projects. articles.title: Assam to become India's first state with its own Earth observation system, AssamSAT
articles.content: Home Trending News Assam to become India’s first state with its own Earth observation system, AssamSAT Assam to become India’s first state with its own Earth observation system, AssamSAT Assam is set to become India’s first state to have its own Earth observation system, AssamSAT. The government of Assam is currently in the final stage of selecting a private partner for the mission. By Devanshu Srivastava 26 Aug 2026 Follow Us New Update Assam to become India’s first state with its own Earth observation system, AssamSAT The Assam government is in the final stage of selecting a private-sector partner to develop AssamSAT, its proposed Earth observation satellite system. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the state is moving ahead with the project, which aims to make Assam the first state in India to have its own dedicated Earth observation system. According to Sarma, AssamSAT will be developed under the ‘DBLOTT model’, which stands for Design, Build, Launch, Operate, Train, and Transfer. AssamSAT Project Announced in 2025-26 Budget The AssamSAT project was first announced in the state’s 2025-26 budget in March. Advertisment Add Startup Pedia As A Trusted Source The initiative aims to establish the state’s own satellite system in collaboration with the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) under the Department of Space. “Earlier this year, we invited Expressions of Interest to select an implementation partner under the DBLOTT model. Following strong interest from India's private space sector companies, we are now in the final and critical stage of partner selection, with dedicated committees evaluating the proposals,” Sarma said in a social media post. Satellite Data to Support Key State Operations The project is intended to provide Assam with a continuous and reliable flow of dedicated data from space to manage critical socio-economic projects. The planned applications of AssamSAT include agriculture, flood and disaster management, infrastructure development, border security management, and police and security operations. The Chief Minister further said that the government intends to set up four to five satellites, with different satellites covering different parts of the state. A command centre will also be established in Guwahati. The CM further said that the government intends to set up 4-5 satellites, with different satellites covering different parts of the state and a command centre in its capital, Guwahati. He added that ‘AssamSAT’ would mark a shift from Assam being a user of satellite data to an active participant in the space-tech ecosystem. It will enable faster and more efficient governance in the state. 13 Bidders Show Interest in AssamSAT Sarma said AssamSAT would mark a shift from Assam being a user of satellite data to becoming an active participant in the space-tech ecosystem. The system is expected to enable faster and more efficient governance in the state. So far, 13 bidders have shown interest in the project. These include established aerospace and defence companies such as BEL , Tata Advanced Systems, Ananth Technologies and Data Patterns. articles.content: PRNewswire Gurugram (Haryana) [India], August 26: IntelliDB Enterprise, India's first AI-Powered database management platform, today announced a strategic partnership with Yotta Data Services, a leading Indian provider of sovereign cloud, AI infrastructure and hyperscale data centre services to deliver sovereign, AI-ready database infrastructure hosted on Yotta's sovereign cloud and AI infrastructure in India. The partnership is aimed at enterprises, government organizations, and regulated industries looking to modernize database infrastructure and build AI applications while ensuring complete data sovereignty and regulatory compliance. Together, the companies will offer fully managed database services hosted on Yotta's sovereign cloud infrastructure, enabling enterprises to modernize mission-critical workloads while maintaining complete data sovereignty and regulatory compliance. IntelliDB's platform is built on PostgreSQL's engine which is one of the world's most widely used database technologies with IntelliDB's own core features and AI capabilities. What IntelliDB Brings to the Table IntelliDB Enterprise is built to make databases secure, scalable and smarter to run. IntelliDB already meets some of the toughest data protection and security standards used by hospitals, banks, and global businesses, including HIPAA, GDPR, SOC-1, SOC-2, and PCI-DSS, giving customers a headstart on compliance rather than a project to build it from scratch. Why This Matters More companies want to use Artificial Intelligence in their everyday software, but AI tools need a database that can keep up, one that's fast, secure, and able to understand the meaning behind information, not just store it. By combining IntelliDB's database platform with Yotta's sovereign cloud and AI infrastructure, businesses can now build these AI-powered applications without sending sensitive data outside the country and meeting India's data protection requirements by design, not as an afterthought. Together, IntelliDB and Yotta provide organizations with an integrated platform that combines intelligent database management with secure, scalable and sovereign infrastructure for enterprise AI and data-intensive applications. This partnership allows customers to: * Run AI-powered applications on a database built for them, hosted on Yotta's sovereign cloud infrastructure. * Get a fully managed database service, so internal IT teams spend less time on day-to-day maintenance. * Meet strict data protection and compliance standards without building that capability from scratch. * Modernize older data infrastructure using IntelliDB's specialised migration toolkit on Yotta's secure, sovereign cloud infrastructure. * Grow from everyday business applications to advanced AI applications on the same platform. articles.title: SkinBB Goes Live with India's First Audited Skincare Intelligence Platform bringing AI ... - ANI News
articles.content: VMPL Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], August 26: India's skincare industry is witnessing an information boom, but consumer confidence has not kept pace. As millions of online voices compete to influence skincare choices, consumers are left navigating a maze of ingredient claims, product recommendations, and conflicting advice. Addressing this challenge, Skin Beyond Borders (SkinBB) today announced the public launch of India's first independently audited, dermatologist-driven skincare ecosystem and marketplace. This integrated Skin Intelligence Ecosystem combines AI-powered technology, dermatologist-led expertise, and scientific product curation to help consumers make informed skincare decisions based on evidence rather than trends. Built specifically for Indian skin, climate, and consumer needs, the platform combines multiple proprietary technologies into a single ecosystem designed to simplify skincare while improving confidence in every decision. Commenting on the launch, Ajit Marathe, Founder of SkinBB, said, "The biggest challenge in skincare today is not access to information -- it is knowing what to trust. Every intelligence layer this industry needs already exists in India, in isolation, generating data every day that no one has been positioned to connect. SkinBB is the connective tissue. Today's launch is the first step towards building a predictive intelligence layer for the Indian skincare industry -- one where environmental patterns, ingredient behaviour, dermatological consensus and consumer experience inform each other continuously. In this first release, that means personalised, credentialled guidance for the consumer, delivered under a single operating principle: the intelligence informs; the consumer decides." Most skincare marketplaces list what brands submit. Claims like "dermatologist-tested" or "clinically proven" accompany the product to the point of sale, leaving the consumer without a way to verify them. The marketplace itself has had no mechanism either. SkinBB inverts that sequence. Every product listed on the platform is reviewed through its independent Product Review and Advisory Council (PRAC) before it becomes available. The council evaluates products for ingredient safety, label compliance, and claim integrity. Only products that meet the standard are listed. This matters beyond the listing itself. Every downstream layer of the platform depends on it--a personalised ingredient score is only as reliable as the product data it is scored against. By verifying products at the point of entry rather than flagging them after the fact, PRAC establishes the foundation on which the rest of the ecosystem's intelligence rests. At the heart of the platform is VyBIE, SkinBB's Living Skin Intelligence engine, which combines an individual's skin profile with hyperlocal environmental conditions, including UV radiation, air quality, temperature, and humidity, to generate contextual skincare guidance. VyBIE provides tailored skincare insights based on users' locations and environmental factors, translating complex data into practical guidance. Supporting this experience is the Skin Friendliness Index (SFI), a proprietary model for environmental skin health score that integrates UV exposure, air quality, temperature, and humidity into a single indicator reflecting how favourable the surrounding environment is for skin health. Designed to provide a holistic assessment of environmental exposure, SFI ensures that severe environmental risks are never masked by otherwise favourable conditions. articles.title: Nexus Select CITYWALK to Host India's First KidRox Fitness and Obstacle Experience for Children
articles.content: Events Industry Watch Articles News Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Nexus Select CITYWALK in Delhi is set to host India’s first KidRox, a three-day fitness and obstacle experience designed for children aged 2–10 years. The event will take place from August 28 to 30, offering children and families an opportunity to participate in active, screen-free experiences. Built around the philosophy “Race. Sweat. Smile. Repeat.”, KidRox aims to encourage children to step away from screens and discover the joy of movement through play, challenges and interactive activities. The experience is centred around five core pillars — Run, Challenge, Play, Achieve and Share. It will feature running circuits, coordination and balance obstacles, as well as interactive play zones designed to make physical activity engaging for young children. KidRox follows a non-competitive format, focusing on participation and personal achievement rather than finishing first. Children will be encouraged to run, jump, crawl, balance and navigate different obstacles in a supportive environment where every milestone can be celebrated. The experience also encourages families to participate together, allowing children to enjoy an active day with parents, siblings and friends. Beyond the main obstacle course, KidRox will bring together fitness, wellness, nutrition, activities, shopping, food and entertainment. Visitors will be able to explore interactive brand experiences, wellness and nutrition zones and activities designed for children and families. One of the key highlights will be the KidRox Bazaar, a curated space where families can discover children’s brands, products, activities and experiences. The bazaar will add another dimension to the event, allowing families to explore products and experiences while taking part in the wider KidRox programme. With KidRox, Nexus Select CITYWALK continues its focus on creating family-oriented experiences that bring people together while encouraging children to embrace active, healthy and playful lifestyles. The three-day experience will combine obstacle challenges, active play, family activities and interactive experiences, giving children an opportunity to build confidence, try new activities and celebrate their achievements in a fun environment.

articles.title: NODWIN Gaming Announces SpaceFest, India's First Dedicated Space , Science and Sci-Fi Festival
articles.content: Events Industry Watch Articles News Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp NODWIN Gaming has announced the launch of SpaceFest, positioned as India’s first large-scale festival dedicated to space, science, innovation and space-inspired pop culture. The initiative is backed by the Government of Maharashtra and was announced at a press conference held at Trident, Mumbai, on August 26, 2026. SpaceFest aims to bring together global space leaders, space-tech startups, policymakers, creators, students and space enthusiasts on a common platform that combines knowledge, innovation and entertainment. The press conference was attended by Hon’ble Minister Dr. Uday Samant, Industries, Investment and Services Department; Dr. P Anbalagan, IAS, Principal Secretary (Industries, Investment & Services), Government of Maharashtra; Shri Deependra Singh Kushwah, IAS, CEO of MIDC Mumbai; Aarti Harbhajanka, Co-Founder and MD, Primus Partners India; and Akshat Rathee, Co-founder and Managing Director, NODWIN Gaming, who conceptualised the IP. Inspired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision for India’s space economy, SpaceFest is being developed as a platform to celebrate space exploration, innovation and discovery. It will also provide Maharashtra’s space-tech startups with opportunities to showcase their innovations, build partnerships and connect with global industry leaders and investors. Speaking at the press conference, Guest of Honour Uday Samant said, “For me, space was always associated with missions like Chandrayaan and the achievements of ISRO and NASA. But SpaceFest has made me realise the immense interest and potential this sector holds, especially among India’s students and youth. I am proud that Maharashtra is taking the lead with this initiative. I propose that Space Fest be held in February, giving us more time to create employment opportunities and strengthen the ecosystem. Our vision is to position Maharashtra not only as a leader in India’s space sector, but as a global space hub. The space economy has the potential to generate lakhs of crores, and we are committed to bringing a significant share of this opportunity to Maharashtra. We will take every step necessary to make this vision a reality.” Dr. P Anbalagan IAS, Principal Secretary (Industries, Investment & Services), Government of Maharashtra, unveiled the SpaceFest launch video and expressed his support for the initiative. He said, “Nearly 25% of India’s aerospace, defence and navigation systems are manufactured in Maharashtra, and the state is also the first to have an independent aerospace policy that includes space technology. With India’s space-tech sector currently valued at around $8.5–9 billion and projected to reach $100 billion by 2040, the opportunity is significant. For any sector to grow, it needs the right ecosystem of stakeholders, agencies, international institutions, R&D and capital. articles.title: India's First Bullet Train Corridor Gains Momentum As 74 Km Of Piers Ready For Viaduct ...
articles.content: India’s First Bullet Train Corridor Gains Momentum As 74 Km Of Piers Ready For Viaduct Girders In Maharashtra India’s first bullet train corridor has achieved major construction progress in Maharashtra’s Thane-Palghar section, with 74 km of piers ready for viaduct girders. NHSRCL said work is underway on over 100 km of elevated structures, while three of seven mountain tunnels have achieved breakthroughs. Major river bridges and stations at Thane, Virar and Boisar are also under construction. Add FPJ As a Trusted Source Abhishek Pathak Updated: Wednesday, August 26, 2026, 01:18 AM IST India’s First Bullet Train Corridor Gains Momentum As 74 Km Of Piers Ready For Viaduct Girders In Maharashtra | File Photo Mumbai: India's first Bullet Train corridor is making rapid progress across the challenging terrain of Thane and Palghar, with 74 km of piers now ready to receive viaduct girders and construction underway on more than 100 km of the elevated section. Three of the seven mountain tunnels have also achieved breakthrough, while work on major river bridges is progressing along the 135.45-km stretch from Shilphata in Thane to Zaroli on the Maharashtra-Gujarat border. Maharashtra section spans 135 km The section forms part of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor and includes 124.027 km of viaducts and bridges. Construction is underway at the three elevated stations planned at Thane, Virar and Boisar. At Thane, the station concourse is being built around 12 metres above the natural ground level to help preserve mangroves in the eco-sensitive area. The construction involves several technically demanding structures. Of the seven mountain tunnels in the section, three have already achieved breakthrough, with drainage, waterproofing and tunnel-lining work now progressing. Major bridges are also being built across the Ulhas River (460 metres), Vaitarna River (2.32 km) and Jagani River (510 metres). The pace of work marks a shift from foundation and pier construction towards the next stage of placing viaduct girders. With the corridor passing through urban areas, rivers, highways, railway lines, hills and ecologically sensitive zones, the Thane-Palghar section remains among the technically diverse stretches of the project. articles.title: Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet train project construction work making rapid progress: NHSRCL - ET Infra
articles.content: Railways 1 min read Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet train project construction work making rapid progress: NHSRCL Work is progressing on a 135.45-km elevated stretch in Maharashtra, with 74 km of piers completed and three tunnels achieving breakthrough. PTI Published On Aug 26, 2026 at 10:07 AM IST Select ETInfra as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Construction work underway on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor across Thane and Palghar districts. Construction work on India's first bullet train project is making rapid headway across the scenic terrains of Thane and Palghar districts in Maharashtra, according to an official release by the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited ( NHSRCL ) on Tuesday. Sharing glimpses of ongoing progress, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw highlighted the key achievements across the 135.45 km-long elevated stretch, which spans from Shilphata in Thane district to Zaroli village on the Maharashtra-Gujarat border. Advt "The 135.45 km section includes 124.027 km of viaducts and bridges, connecting the high-speed rail corridor across varied terrain," the release stated. It said work is actively progressing on three elevated stations at Thane, Virar, and Boisar. The Thane station has been specially engineered with its concourse level approximately 12 metres above natural ground level to protect and preserve local mangroves in the eco-sensitive zone. Pier construction is underway across more than 100 km, with nearly 74 km of piers already complete and ready for viaduct girders. To support this scale, 9 casting yards, 7 full-span launching gantries, and 8 SBS launching gantries are currently operational in Maharashtra, it added. Out of the seven planned mountain tunnels along this section, 3 have already achieved breakthrough, with drainage, waterproofing, and lining works now in progress. Furthermore, major river bridges are under construction over the Ulhas River (460 metres), Vaitarna River (2.32 km), and Jagani River (510 metres). The project features 36 bridges and crossings, including 12 steel bridges spanning major railway lines, the Mumbai-Nashik Highway, and the Ulhas River. The ongoing momentum reflects the engineering precision behind the project under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw's drive to expand next-generation railway infrastructure, the release stated. articles.title: Chhattisgarh launches India's first official state hockey league, six teams to battle for trophy
articles.content: Sports 26 Aug, 2026 Chhattisgarh launches India's first official state hockey league, six teams to battle for trophy Business To Business, Raipur, 26 August 2026: Chhattisgarh is set to host India's first official state-level hockey league under the aegis of Hockey India, with the inaugural Chhattisgarh Hockey League (CHL) scheduled to be held from October 21 to November 1 at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Hockey Stadium in Raipur. The franchise-based league, announced by the Sports and Youth Welfare Department of Chhattisgarh on Tuesday, will feature six teams representing different regions of the state. Indian hockey stalwarts and Olympic medallists Gurjant Singh, Shamsher Singh and Surender Kumar have been named among the marquee players for the inaugural edition. Other prominent Indian team players, including Jaskaran Singh and Devindar Walmiki, will also be part of the league. The official logo, mascot and identities of the six participating teams were unveiled at an event attended by Chhattisgarh Deputy Chief Minister and Sports and Youth Welfare Minister Arun Sao, along with senior officials from the department and Hockey Chhattisgarh. "Chhattisgarh has a very strong base in terms of athletes across sports, and it is an honour to be the first state to introduce an official state hockey league. This reinforces our commitment towards the national game and is a testament to the effort that the Department of Sports and Youth Welfare has been putting in over the years. Chhattisgarh Hockey League marks a very important starting point in what can promise to be an extremely flourishing addition to the history of Indian Hockey. The main aim has always been to provide the state’s athletes with the best opportunity to excel at the state, national and international level, and we are sure that the CHL is a step in the right direction towards that," said Sao. The league will follow a round-robin format, with the top four teams advancing to the semifinals. The semifinals will be played as knock-out matches, while the final is scheduled for November 1. A special exhibition match between women's teams is also planned on the day of the final. The six franchises unveiled for the inaugural season are Rajdhani Royals, Chitrakoot Challengers, Sanskardhani Strikers, Chakradhar Champions, Nyayadhani Knights and Mainpat Titans. The league's visual identity features the map of Chhattisgarh alongside a stylized hockey player, highlighting regional pride and the state's connection with the sport. The saffron and green elements represent an Indian identity, while the orange trail symbolizes energy, speed and ambition. The official mascot, Baghwa, a tiger, was also unveiled. The mascot represents courage, strength and resilience while drawing inspiration from Chhattisgarh's forests and rich wildlife heritage. The league will carry the tagline "Chalo Re Sangi, Hockey Khelbo", reflecting the state's sporting identity and passion for hockey.
